resources.string: Ruru is looking for the Bose headphones this iPhone is playing through.

Ruru connects to the Bose headphones this iPhone is playing through. Connect them in Settings > Bluetooth. If iPhone asks to pair them with Ruru, choose Pair. After the Bose app has used them, they can take a few minutes to show up. If you renamed them in iPhone Settings, change the name back. Ruru connects by itself.
Ruru looks for a paired Bluetooth device with Bose in its name. Pair your headphones in this phone's Bluetooth settings. If you renamed them, put Bose back in their name. Ruru connects by itself.
Ruru looks for a paired Bluetooth device with Bose in its name. Pair your headphones in this computer's Bluetooth settings. If you renamed them, put Bose back in their name. Ruru connects by itself.
Turn the headphones on, or put them on if they've gone to sleep. If they connect to another device first, choose this phone in their Bluetooth list. Ruru connects by itself.

Ruru needs Android's Nearby devices permission to see your paired headphones. Allow it in Android's settings for Ruru, then come back.
Allow Bluetooth when iPhone asks. Ruru uses it only to talk to your headphones.

Ruru has not been tested on this model yet. If something looks wrong, a connection report helps.
These headphones use Bose's older app (Bose Connect). Ruru shows their battery only.
These earbuds use the separate Bose QC Earbuds app. Ruru can't control them.
Basic support: battery, equaliser, settings and the noise cancelling level. These headphones have no listening modes.
Basic support: battery, equaliser, settings, the noise cancelling level and switching modes. Saving your own modes is untested on these earbuds.

Ruru is free. If it helps you, you can shout the developer a coffee on Ko-fi.
Opens in the tray when you sign in
Closing the window leaves Ruru in the tray so your headphones stay connected. Turn this off to quit Ruru when you close the window.
Ruru is still running in the tray. You can change this in Settings.
